authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: The plain-attack DDoS-to-Benign rate exceeded the paired clean rate; the defended rate was lower than the plain-attack rate. Attribution distance decreased after reconstruction, but oracle-clean recovery was not established.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.329128 versus 0.040246 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.042709, an absolute reduction of 0.286420 from the plain attack branch.
Mean malicious recall was 0.975000; minimum malicious recall was 0.900000; maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.000000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.753257 to 0.467583, with recovery fraction 0.379252.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert verified malicious intent: the evidence does not establish it.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery: an oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable and exact recovery is unsupported.
Refuse to make client-flagging, threshold, trust-weight, reconstruction, or aggregation decisions.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator was the paired round 4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable and were not substituted.
Per-client detector scores and numeric detector thresholds were not present.
Evidence was limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
